summary: Implemented as automatic behaviour rather than a manual control, at the product owner's direction: with the full graph visible, radii follow producer record counts (the default the proposal asked to preserve); the moment any kind is switched off in the legend, every remaining node is re-sized by its count of DISTINCT visible neighbours in the retained subgraph — hiding a kind literally subtracts its connections from what remains. Degree is computed only from producer-supplied edges already on the canvas whose endpoints both survive the filters (no inference, no refetch); nonzero floor r=3 for visible isolated nodes; same scale as records sizing. Radii rescale with a 320ms transition scoped to the rescale moment only (an is-resizing class, ~400ms) so no transitions run during load or simulation settle, plus a mild reheat (alpha 0.25). Landmark labels now rank by current radius, so the biggest nodes in a filtered view carry their names. While filtered sizing is active the status line reads 'sizes now rank by connections among what you kept — bounded to this canvas, not complete totals'. Restoring all kinds returns producer-count sizing exactly. Verified live on Valparai at 1440x1000: keeping only recorded names and places re-ranks correctly (the two mapped-square places largest, then the names recorded at the most places); zero refetches; reset restores records sizing; search, isolation, cards and decluttering unchanged.
consumer_note: The explicit two-mode control shipped first, but the product owner asked for the sizing to follow the legend chips automatically, so the control was removed — 'size by connections' is now the meaning of filtering itself. Note for the future extension: because ambient edges are a sample and expansions are capped per relation, on-canvas degree is directionally honest but cannot support exact claims like 'A has 10x more connections than B'. If the producer ships complete per-node degree summaries (per kind-pair), the consumer can size filtered views from exact totals with no interaction change.
